title: Tyler, 27: Paying the Minimum on $4,500

scenes.say: Paying only the minimum, Tyler's $4,500 card takes about 18 years.
His card charges about 23%. His first minimum is around $131.
But as the balance drops, the minimum shrinks too, so the debt crawls.
He'd pay about $12,000 in total. Roughly $7,500 is interest.
The fix is boring: keep paying $131, even when the minimum drops.
That clears it in under 5 years, with about $2,900 of interest.
Push it to $250 a month, and he's free in 2 years, paying about $1,100.
Do you pay the minimum or a fixed amount? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, because $4,500 shouldn't take 18 years.

question: Do you pay the minimum or a fixed amount on your card?
description: Tyler owes about $4,500 on a card at roughly 23% APR. Paying only the shrinking minimum (interest plus 1%) takes about 18 years and around $7,500 of interest. Locking the payment at $131 cuts it to under 5 years, and $250 a month to about 2 years. Rounded estimates assuming a fixed APR and no new charges.
